newsitem.title: USA: Judge OKs $75 mln Sacramento, Calif., arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Judge OKs $75 mln Sacramento, Calif., arena deal.

text.p: A Superior Court judge ruled on Thursday in favor of Sacramento's $75 million plan to refinance its basketball arena, clearing the way for the city to enter the market with notes for the deal, attorneys for the city said.

Sacramento County Superior Court Judge John Stroud ruled that the city's proposed note financing was legal, eliminating court challenges that had threatened to scuttle the arena deal, the attorneys said.
The Sacramento City Council approved the note plan in February to keep the National Basketball Association's Sacramento Kings from leaving the city.
With the proceeds of the note sale, the city would refinance $51.5 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining note proceeds would be used to refinance other franchise debts.

The notes were expected to be sold in April. But the deal was put on hold after lawsuits were filed to block the plan. The lawsuits alleged that the collateral for the arena deal was "inadequate," and that the plan violated state tax rules.

In its nine page ruling Thursday, the court said it "validates" the deal. "The court has no power to question the economic or governmental wisdom of the city council in legislative matters such as these," Stroud wrote.

The judge ruled that the proposed financing would not violate state tax rules and rejected allegations the deal "circumvented" California's Proposition 218, which requires voter-approval of new taxes.
Attorneys for the city welcomed the ruling and said it should allow Sacramento to come to market with the arena notes in the coming weeks.
"The city is very pleased with the decision and we are looking forward to getting the judgment entered as quickly as possible," said city attorney Norman Hile.
